title: Feedback Loops are All You Need — Mehedi Hassan, Granola
talk_summary: A product engineer at Granola describes how they made LLM behavior debuggable by building custom tracing tooling that logs every tool call, cost, and reasoning step to a DB with a UI for non-engineers, and how they converted their Electron renderer into a web shell so CI produces preview links that agents can self-verify with screenshots. The core thesis is that one-shotting better is not the answer; closing fast feedback loops (observability plus testable previews) is.

takeaways.technique: Custom agent-loop tracing UI over a DB
takeaways.what_they_do: They wrap the AI SDK, persist every tool call, reasoning step, and cost to a database, and build a UI structured for their own team (product, data, CX, not just engineers) so anyone can replay an agent loop front-to-back and see exactly where it failed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we essentially just like save things to a DB, wrap around like AI SDK, and then the front-end is like kind of like the most important part

takeaways.technique: Web-shell preview links for agent self-verification
takeaways.what_they_do: They abstracted Electron IPC and React APIs to web standards so the renderer runs as a web app; every PR now gets a preview link, and Cursor opens it, tests the change, and uploads a screenshot to the PR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once we open a PR, Cursor goes and tests it, uploads a screenshot into our PRs, which speeds up the testing so much more

takeaways.what_they_do: Because the app is testable via a URL, the coding agent verifies its own work (runs the app, screenshots) before review, so reviewers see evidence rather than claims.
takeaways.evidence_quote: because LLMs can now self-verify their work

takeaways.technique: Own the search/tool layer instead of provider built-ins
takeaways.what_they_do: They found provider web-search tools blow up context and cost (~10p/chat) and can silently degrade on provider updates, so they want control over the search pipeline rather than a one-line tool add.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each chat could be costing you like 10 pence
takeaways.numbers: ~10 pence per chat with provider web search

takeaways.technique: Parallel variant testing via preview environments
takeaways.what_they_do: They use cheap one-shotting to generate multiple feature variants and test them in parallel through web previews instead of serially in a single local Electron instance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can experiment with like one feature looking very different in four different users
